rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Now you are the one reading. Each written move says which piece to move and where to.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: Remember the letters: K is the king, Q the queen, R the rook, B the bishop and N the knight.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: N is the knight. Nf3 means: the knight goes to the f3 square.
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! Nf3, one of the most common moves in chess.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The knight jumps from g1 to f3. That is Nf3.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.g1h3.1: That is Nh3: the h3 square is on the last file. The move asks for f3.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.g1h3.2: Let's go back: look for the letter f on the bottom edge.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: The knight went to another square. Let's go back: the target is f3.
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: Only one knight could reach f3, so the letter and the square are enough.
rot.ideia.ex1.l2: Remember the idea: read the letter to find the piece and the square to find the destination.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: Castling has its own notation. Short castling, with the king on g1 and the rook on f1, is O-O.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: Long castling, with the king on c1 and the rook on d1, is O-O-O. As always, you only move the king.
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! O-O-O: the king on c1 and the rook on d1.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The king moves two squares to c1, and the rook jumps to d1. That is O-O-O.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.e1g1.1: That is short castling, O-O, with two Os. The move asks for three: O-O-O.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.e1g1.2: Let's go back: O-O-O is towards the rook on a1.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: That move is not castling. Let's go back: in castling, the king moves two squares.
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: Remember the idea: O-O is short castling; O-O-O, long castling.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: Now I will show how to read a whole game and two special cases.
rot.demos.partida.e1: In a game, each number has two moves: White's and then Black's.
rot.demos.partida.l1: 1. e4: the white pawn goes to e4.
rot.demos.partida.l2: e5: Black replies with the pawn on e5. That ends the first move.
rot.demos.partida.l3: 2. Nf3: the white knight comes out and attacks the pawn.
rot.demos.partida.l4: Nc6: the black knight protects the pawn. Written: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6.
rot.demos.doisCavalos.e1: Sometimes two identical pieces can go to the same square. Both knights reach d2.
rot.demos.doisCavalos.l1: Only then do you write the file the piece came from: Nbd2, the knight on the b-file.
rot.demos.promocao.e1: In a promotion, you write the square, an equals sign and the letter of the new piece.
rot.demos.promocao.l1: The pawn reaches e8 and is promoted to a queen: e8=Q.
rot.demos.promocao.l2: Now it's your turn: in the next positions, I write the moves and you play them.
rot.pratica.peao.enunciado: The pawn has no letter. Play e4.
rot.pratica.peao.fim: Perfect. e4, the most famous move in chess.
rot.pratica.peao.err.e2e3: That is e3. The move asks for e4: the pawn moves two squares. Try again.
rot.pratica.abertura.enunciado: Play White: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4. I will make Black's moves.
rot.pratica.abertura.fim: Well done. You read a whole opening, move by move.
rot.pratica.roque.fim: Done: you can read and write moves. This is the language I use in the lessons.
